clue.text: Dobson reportedly ready for the Swiss?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Frank Dobson, the Labour minister of the time

explanation.surface: A satirical question about whether Frank Dobson is fit for Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' says Frank, the first name of Frank Dobson (Labour's Health Secretary in the late 1990s), is heard as the Swiss coin; ready is slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland's currency is this coin, and 'ready' is British slang for cash money.

clue.text: Smooth writer fondled to the end

parts.note: felt is the past tense of feel, to fondle
a tip is the end of something

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking author groped someone all the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen with a fibre point glides easily across paper.

clue.text: Gail, wantonly grasped by another girl, gets some old-fashioned English tongue

indicators.note: grasped by means the jumbled letters go inside the other girl's name

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: wantonly means wildly, so the letters of Gail are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gail, groped by another woman, gets a taste of old English kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wantonly' scrambles Gail into GLIA and 'grasped by' wraps another girl's name round it; 'tongue' hints at kissing but means a language, and 'some' marks it as one of several Old English dialects.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles' dialects of Old English, spoken in Mercia and Northumbria, form this language group.

clue.text: Agreeable schedule helps to keep Brenda and co, going …

definitions.text: helps to keep Brenda and co, going

parts.note: civil means polite and agreeable
a schedule is a list

explanation.surface: A pleasant timetable keeps the Queen and family on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen; this was the parliamentary payment funding the royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual sum voted by Parliament paid for the monarch's official household and duties.

clue.text: Archer's front and superior lip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Archer is Cupid, and a bow is also the front of a ship
second meaning: the curved shape of the upper lip

explanation.walkthrough: Archer suggests Jeffrey Archer, a Private Eye favourite, but here it is Cupid, whose weapon is a bow; 'superior' simply means upper.
explanation.definitionFit: The double curve of the upper lip is named after the shape of the love god's weapon.

clue.text: … keep going to indulge in illicit sex

definitions.meaning: first meaning: continue, following on from the previous clue
second meaning: to have an affair

explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on from the previous clue; the phrasal verb also means conducting an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means continue and, informally, have an extramarital fling.

clue.text: Stalker introduces head of police (city) to plaintiff

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of police

parts.note: P is the first letter of police
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
a plaintiff is one who sues, a suer

explanation.surface: A stalker introduces a senior policeman to a complainant.
explanation.definitionFit: One who stalks follows and hunts a quarry, a chaser.

clue.text: Queer penis pressed against Lewinsky's butt

parts.note: dick is slang for penis

indicators.note: the butt is the end, so the last letter of Lewinsky's

parts.note: Y is the final letter of Lewinsky's name

explanation.surface: A lewd picture of Clinton and Monica Lewinsky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt' means the end, giving the last letter of Lewinsky. Queer is used in its old British sense of unwell or shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal usage calls a weak heart or unsteady state dodgy, the sense of both words.

clue.text: What an arse to jump Brenda

parts.note: to bound is to jump
Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose cipher is ER

explanation.surface: An oaf ready to leap on the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned cad or rotter is exactly the sort of man called an arse.

clue.text: Observe comedian getting head

parts.note: a wit is a clever comedian
ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Orford Ness

explanation.surface: Watch the comic receive oral sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To see an event take place is to be present and watch it.

clue.text: See 17
RUC tire out rookie

indicators.note: out signals the letters of RUC tire are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: The Northern Irish police wear out a new officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals rearranging RUC TIRE; the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the Northern Ireland police of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer or novice enlisted into a force is a fresh member, the same as a rookie.

clue.text: Operetta inaccessible to many if Jack has his way

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera

definitions.text: inaccessible to many if Jack has his way
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Home Secretary Jack Straw planned to restrict the right to this kind of hearing

explanation.walkthrough: In 1999 Jack Straw, then Home Secretary, proposed removing the defendant's right to choose this form of hearing for many offences.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote a one-act comic opera of this name, and it is also the courtroom procedure with twelve citizens deciding.

clue.text: Former government dept's fast breeder

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the old Department of the Environment, known by its initials
second meaning: a female rabbit, famous for breeding quickly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast breeder' sounds like a nuclear reactor, but it is a female rabbit; the 's joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The initials of the abolished ministry spell the name for a female rabbit or deer, a prolific animal.

clue.text: Perhaps Chelsea type holiday accommodation presented to Brenda

parts.note: a pension is a small continental guesthouse
Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose cipher is ER

explanation.surface: Holiday lodgings offered to the Queen, perhaps by a Chelsea sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea Pensioners are retired soldiers living at the Royal Hospital in Chelsea, London, so 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chelsea Pensioner is one instance of a retired person drawing an allowance.

clue.text: Behold a great organ before you

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to look at, as a verb
second meaning: Private ..., the magazine the solver is reading, is called by this word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' sounds anatomical, but it also means a publication, and Private Eye is the organ in front of the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at something closely is to view it, and the magazine is known by this short name.

clue.text: Legislators and where they play with balls, etc.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: peers of the House of ...

definitions.text: where they play with balls, etc.
definitions.meaning: second meaning: ..., the London cricket ground

explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London; the second reading pretends the peers themselves play with balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the upper house of Parliament make laws, and the cricket ground shares their name.

clue.text: Windbag makes flamboyant kisser

parts.note: flamboyant, showy colours are called loud
kisser is slang for the mouth

explanation.surface: A boastful talker turns out to be a showy kisser.
explanation.definitionFit: A windbag talks too much and too noisily, the same as a brash talker.

clue.text: Pissed but not lashing out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for drunk
second meaning: stingy, since lashing out is spending freely

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lashing out' looks violent, but in British usage it means splashing out money.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for drunk and also describes a miser reluctant to spend.

clue.text: Rent low (but rising) from where our saucy columnist reports

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, means the word for low is read upwards

parts.note: low is the sound a cow makes, moo

explanation.surface: A cheap rent, though going up, is written up by a gossip writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearoom is a classic venue for gossip, the stock-in-trade of a saucy columnist.

clue.text: Roger, clear the hurdle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: roger is British slang for having sex
second meaning: literally lifting a limb over a jump

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang for having sex, and taken literally describes stepping over a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom is crude slang for a sexual conquest and also describes straddling an obstacle.

clue.text: About to get limp — that makes a change for certain ministers!

definitions.text: that makes a change for certain ministers

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to limp is to walk with a shuffle

explanation.surface: A minister on the way out starts limping as the Cabinet changes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cabinet shake-up moves ministers to new posts or out of government.

clue.text: Bollocks attached to ring by Rugby Union, note, in this region, down under

parts.note: bollocks is slang for nonsense, rot
a ring is shaped like the letter O
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: Rude talk of a rugby match somewhere in the Antipodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' is Australia and New Zealand; this is a city and district on New Zealand's North Island, fittingly a rugby stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a geothermal district of New Zealand, which Britons call the Antipodes.

clue.text: Flipping outsize Beryl dithered like a judge

indicators.note: flipping turns the abbreviation for outsize over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: dithered means shaken in indecision, so the letters of Beryl are mixed

explanation.surface: A large woman named Beryl hesitated, as a judge might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild curse but turns OS into SO; 'dithered' scrambles BERYL into BERLY. The idiom is 'sober as a judge'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'sober as a judge' links a judge with a steady, abstemious manner.

clue.text: Good spellers, homosexuals, without resorting to PC

definitions.meaning: first meaning: benign spirits who cast spells
second meaning: an old, politically incorrect slang word for gay men

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spellers' suggests people good at spelling, but here they cast spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Magical sprites cast enchantments, and the same word was once a slur for gay men.

clue.text: Intellectual what's got laid by boss!

parts.note: an egg is what a hen lays
the boss is the head of an organisation

explanation.surface: A sly suggestion that a brainy person was bedded by their employer.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an informal term for a bookish, brainy person.

clue.text: Bill accepted Monica finally getting caught

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of Monica

parts.note: A is the last letter of Monica
CT is a cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton took Monica Lewinsky's advances and was finally found out.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary bill that has been passed into law becomes a statute of that name.

clue.text: Military force failing disastrously? That's what this amounts to so often

definitions.text: Military force failing disastrously? That's what this amounts to so often

parts.note: NATO is the Western military alliance
bombing is slang for flopping badly, as a show bombs

explanation.surface: A jibe at the 1999 Kosovo air campaign as a military fiasco.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the satirical comment: the alliance's air campaign of the time is itself read as a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: The alliance's air raids over Kosovo in 1999 were widely mocked as a disastrous campaign.

clue.text: For example Brown is up for a poke

indicators.note: is up, in a down clue, means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown, say, is game for a poke.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown suggests Gordon Brown, then Chancellor, but it is the colour dun; 'is up' reads EG DUN from the bottom of this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A light prod with the elbow is a gentle jab, the same as a poke.

clue.text: Reserved, Elton or Derek somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the phrase Elton or Derek is used

parts.note: the answer runs across the words Elton, or and Derek

explanation.surface: Elton John or some Derek described as shy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' says only part of 'Elton or Derek' is used; 'Reserved' looks like shyness but means booked in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods requested from a supplier but not yet delivered are booked, much as reserved.

clue.text: Boring comedian's act

definitions.meaning: first meaning: humdrum, as an adjective
second meaning: a performer's set piece of material

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like drilling, but it is an adjective for something dull and ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A standup's prepared set is called this, and the word as an adjective means humdrum.

clue.text: Gay holding cane perversely is not doing it for love

indicators.note: holding means the outer word wraps around the rearranged letters

parts.note: gay in its older sense means merry

indicators.note: perversely means the letters of cane are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A man with a cane who is not in it for love, a nod to paid spanking.
explanation.definitionFit: A hireling acts purely for money or reward, never out of affection.

clue.text: She'd love getting screwed wearing stockings

indicators.note: getting screwed means twisted round, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman who would like to be bedded while wearing her stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is an old word for stockings, so someone in hose is clad in hosiery.
